To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

spicamycin induces differentiation of human myleoid leukemia cells and apoptosis in human myeloid and some lymphoid leukemia cells, and that the mechanism may be associated with down‐ regulation of Bcl‐ 2 expression and modulation PML protein.

the differentiation and apoptosis inducing effects of spicamycins and their derivatives, KRN‐5500, are associated with down‐modulation of Bcl2 protein expression and modulation of promyelocyctic leukemia protein.

spicamycin, a novel macrolide antibiotic, induces differentiation and apoptosis in leukemia and lymphoma cells, and that the apoptosis is associated with down‐ regulation of Bcl‐ 2 expression and modulation (disruption) of PML protein, which is a tumor suppressor protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new derivatives of spicamycins and their biological activity.
the study of the mechanism of apoptosis induction in myeloid and/or lymphoid cell lines by the antitumor antibiotics, spicamycins.
the development of novel anticancer agents from microbial metabolites, which are produced by fermentation of actinomycetes and other microorganisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

spicamycin, KRN550 and their derivatives have been found to be potent inducers of apoptosis in a variety of tumor cell lines, and the mechanism of apoptosis induction may be related to the modulation of Bcl‐family protein and PML protein.
spicamycin is an inducer of apoptosis in both myeloid and non‐myeloid cells, and KRN550 is an inducer apoptosis in myeloid cells.
spicamycin is more potent and induces apoptosis more efficiently than KRN550.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spicamycin is an inducer of differentiation, and KRN550O is an apoptosis inducer.
spicamycin is an antitumor antibiotic that induces apoptosis in myeloid and/or lymphoid cells.

the spicamycins are potent inducers of differentiation and inducers of apoptosis in myeloid and/or lymphoid cell lines, and that these compounds may be useful for treatment of myelogenous and lymphoid neoplasm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spicamycin is able to induce apoptosis in myeloid leukemia and lymphoma cell lines.
spicamycin induces apoptosis in myeloid and nonmyeloid cells, and that apoptosis is associated with down‐ regulation of bcl‐2 expression.
spicamycin induces apoptosis in myeloid and some lymphoid cell lines, and this effect is associated with down‐regulated expression of Bcl‐ 2 and PML protein.
